text:
elyse: heads up — support escalation: multiple EU customers reporting large latency spikes (p99 ~1.8–2.6s) on API surface and occasional auth failures. Started ~09:40 UTC. opening thread to triage.

sam: confirmed in dashboards. request rate steady but egress latency from eu-pop-4 shows sawtooth pattern. TLS handshake tail jumped.

support-ops-bot: Customer C452: example report: "/v1/generate returns 200 but takes 2.4s; some requests 403 intermittently." Ticket: #452-APIEU.

dmitri: quick probe results from internal probe ->
```
> curl -w "time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood-inference.eu/v1/generate
time_connect:0.012 time_appconnect:1.432 time_starttransfer:2.401
```

ana: traceroute from eu-pop-4 to us-east egress shows unexpected cross-az hop; looks like some requests are hairpinned to a different POP before TLS. short sample: `traceroute -n 35.199.x.x` -> shows an extra AS path through vendor-bgp-peering.

sam: grabbing packet capture on gateway for window 09:38–09:46. preliminary tcpdump shows repeated SYN, SYN-ACK gaps and TLS ClientHello retransmits. Seems like intermittent packet loss or routing re-pathing at peering.

sre-oncall: can we repro with ICMP/tcp ping from eu-pop-4 replicas? Also check our GSLB latency and DNS TTL behaviour.

elyse: running synthetic probes now:
```
# from eu-pop-4
mtr -z -c 50 api.redwood-inference.eu
```
results show increased latency and occasional packet loss at hop 6 (third-party transit).

dmitri: correlating with DNS: some queries returning different anycast answers -> small fraction hitting eu-pop-7 instead of eu-pop-4. eu-pop-7 under maintenance earlier today (BGP warmup). Could be warmup + short TTL causing oscillation.

ana: customer auth failures (403) may be due to replayed/duplicated requests hitting stale session store in fallback POP. If a request is retried across POPs during TLS handshake, token validation can time out on the backend.

sam: mitigation options: 1) temporarily pin traffic for affected prefixes to eu-pop-4 via routing policy, 2) increase probe weight and failover threshold to avoid bouncing, 3) route a small fraction to eu-pop-8 as a fallback with warmed cache. Which is fastest?

sre-oncall: do 1 + 3. pinning is fastest to reduce flapping; spin up warmed route to eu-pop-8 so we can shift traffic if pinned POP degrades. Also raise health-check sensitivity to avoid hitting POP repeatedly.

elyse: actioning now — applying temporary routing policy to pin customer C452 prefixes to eu-pop-4 for 15m. also triggering warmup for eu-pop-8 and incrementing GSLB flapping threshold from 2 -> 6.

support-ops-bot: Noted mitigation: routing pin + warm-up. Informed customer C452.

dmitri: monitoring dashboards: after pinning p99 dropped from ~2.1s -> 480ms within 2m. TLS time_appconnect now ~120ms.

ana: leaving capture running; will collect full packet logs for postmortem. We should also check vendor peering logs with network ops to see if they had transient route changes.

sre-oncall: next steps: 1) request peering route dump from provider, 2) analyze DNS TTL + GSLB logs for anomalies at 09:38–09:46, 3) add a one-off Canary test that stresses TLS handshakes across eu POPs. Assigning owners: dmitri (peering logs), ana (dns/gslb), elyse (canary).

elyse: noted. I'll also prepare a customer-facing incident summary if this reoccurs.

sam: quick note — consider adding handshake tail to our per-route SLO dashboard so we can alert earlier on TLS p99.

elyse: agreed. logging this for follow-up in postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:
